html:
Taiwan is an island off the southeast coast of China. The map shows it in 1492 and 1500, again in 1880, and from 1945 on, under very different rulers each time.

  • Before the 1600s it belonged to its indigenous peoples, who speak Austronesian languages, with no outside state in control.
  • 1624 to 1662: the Dutch East India Company ruled the southwest as Dutch Formosa and brought in Chinese farmers.
  • 1662 to 1683: Koxinga, a Ming loyalist, expelled the Dutch and his family ruled the Kingdom of Tungning.
  • 1683 to 1895: the Qing ruled it, at first as part of Fujian and from the 1880s as a province. Chinese settlers became the majority.
  • 1895 to 1945: Japan took Taiwan after beating China in war and made it a model colony, with railways, schools and sugar.
  • From 1945: the Republic of China took over. In 1949, losing the civil war, Chiang Kai-shek and his government retreated to Taiwan with between one and two million soldiers and civilians.

Under martial law, from 1949 to 1987, the Kuomintang party ruled alone while the island grew rich making goods for export. Free elections followed in the 1990s. Today Taiwan is a democracy and the world's leading maker of advanced chips, led by TSMC. Its status remains the main unresolved question between it, the People's Republic of China and the United States.
